title: Add CI validation for Terraform modules (fmt/validate/tflint/checkov) + gating rules
creator: Irene Choi
description:
Context
We’re publishing alpha Terraform modules for Redwood Private (AWS VPC). We need a repeatable CI baseline that enforces formatting, correctness, and minimum security posture so Solutions Eng can confidently hand modules to design partners without introducing avoidable drift or risky defaults.

Scope
Implement CI checks in the redwood-terraform repo:
- terraform fmt (enforce)
- terraform validate (enforce)
- tflint (enforce with agreed rule set)
- checkov (enforce with curated policy + documented exceptions)
- Provider/Terraform version pinning validation (fail if missing/loose)
- Gating rules + required approvals for security-sensitive changes

Acceptance criteria
1) All PRs must run:
   - terraform fmt -check -recursive
   - terraform validate (per module + examples)
   - tflint with repo config (no ad-hoc local rules)
   - checkov scan on modules + examples
2) CI fails on:
   - fmt diffs
   - terraform validate failures
   - tflint errors (warnings allowed only if explicitly configured)
   - checkov HIGH/CRITICAL findings unless:
     a) documented in code with a reason + expiry/owner, and
     b) allowlisted in policy file with ticket link
3) CI output is readable:
   - includes a short “how to fix” hint for the common failures (fmt/tflint/checkov)
   - artifacts uploaded for checkov report (SARIF or JSON) for audit/review
4) Gating/approvals:
   - CODEOWNERS updated to require Security Engineering review for IAM/logging/security-group modules (Marcus Lin or Hanae Suzuki as codeowners)
   - Protect default branch: require CI to pass + at least 1 codeowner approval for affected paths
5) Rollout plan:
   - Phase 1 (1 week): run tflint/checkov in “comment-only”/non-blocking mode to measure noise and tune
   - Phase 2: enforce tflint + checkov gating, with documented exceptions list
   - Phase 3: add “nightly” job for heavier scans across all examples (keeps PR runtime reasonable)

Implementation notes / decisions
- We will standardize on Terraform versions as per infra standards (alpha): pin Terraform + AWS provider in required_providers. CI validates these pins aren’t broadened (e.g., avoid >= without upper bounds).
- checkov baseline: focus on network exposure, logging defaults, encryption-at-rest, and least privilege. We expect some false positives for VPC resources; exceptions must be explicit and time-bounded.
- tflint rules: enable AWS plugin and basic correctness/security rules; avoid style-only rules that create churn during alpha.

Links
- ADR-028 Validation & integration test strategy: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-028-validation-and-integration-test-strategy-for-terraform.json
- CI/CD pipeline design doc: sources/confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/terraform-modules-ci-pipeline.json
- Repo PR (provider pinning + scanners): sources/github/redwood-terraform/pr-18503-add-tflint-checkov-and-provider-version-pinning.json

Task breakdown
- [x] Add GitHub Actions workflow(s) for fmt/validate
- [x] Add tflint config + plugin installation
- [x] Add checkov config + curated policies + output artifacts
- [x] Add CODEOWNERS + branch protection guidance in CONTRIBUTING
- [x] Document how to run locally (make targets)
- [x] Run on existing modules/examples and address failures or add justified exceptions

Rollout / comms
- Announce in #eng-infra and #eng-security once Phase 2 enforcement flips on.
- During alpha, if a design partner needs a temporary exception, exceptions require:
  - ticket + owner + expiry date (<= 30 days)
  - Security Engineering approval (Marcus Lin) for any exception affecting IAM or public exposure.
comments: 2025-06-19 (Sahana Iyer): Drafted workflow plan. Splitting into two jobs: (1) fast PR checks (fmt/validate/tflint) and (2) security scan (checkov) with SARIF upload. Will keep total PR runtime < ~8 minutes by scanning only modules/ + examples/ paths changed. Nightly will scan full tree.

2025-06-21 (Marcus Lin): For alpha, OK to gate on HIGH/CRITICAL only. Please require explicit inline skip annotations with justification + link to Linear issue, not just a global allowlist. Also add CODEOWNERS for modules/iam/** and modules/security-groups/**.

2025-06-24 (Irene Choi): +1 on keeping PR checks quick. If nightly uncovers systemic issues, we’ll open follow-up tickets rather than breaking everyone’s PR flow. Ensure validate runs per module; we’ve had issues where root validate passes but module-level fails due to missing providers.

2025-06-28 (Sahana Iyer): Phase 1 complete (non-blocking). Noise: checkov flagged VPC Flow Logs destination configuration in examples; adding explicit encryption + retention notes + a single scoped skip for one example with documented reason. TFLint caught unused variables in endpoints module—fixed in same PR.
2025-07-03 (Hanae Suzuki): Reviewed CODEOWNERS + checkov exception format. Please add expiry date as a comment adjacent to any skip, and include owner handle/name. Approved after that tweak.

2025-07-08 (Sahana Iyer): Enforcement flipped on for tflint + checkov (HIGH/CRITICAL). Added make targets: make fmt, make validate, make tflint, make checkov. Updated CONTRIBUTING with troubleshooting for common failures. PR runtime ~6–7 min average.

2025-07-11 (Irene Choi): Marking Done. Next: evaluate whether we want to gate on MEDIUM for IAM-related findings in GA; for alpha keep as-is to avoid churn. Follow-up ticket to add scheduled weekly dependency scanning + provider lockfile consistency checks.
